limitations: Fixed seed 42, six bearings and three distances; arbitrary desktop placement is not guaranteed
Historical headless benchmark predates this foraging repair and excludes GUI and startup
Sensory contrast encoding, neural output lookup, and body search are engineered adapters, not validated biological food-seeking behavior
Current hunger cycle uses model time, fixed seed 42 and a new second food; it does not validate biological hunger or food memory
Current satiety can leave food uneaten; historical full-depletion results predate hunger
Associative food memory adjusts virtual odor gains outside the fixed connectome; it is not biological synaptic plasticity.
Population resident memory is peak process memory with four engines allocated; runtime factors exclude GUI and startup.

The two-food assay uses two half-full foods. FlyWire chooses banana both before and after training; Male CNS changes from banana to berry. These fixed-seed results show modulation, not improved preference or biological learning.
Male CNS includes a late contact at 29.666 seconds with only 0.002145 consumption by the 30-second cutoff. Contact success does not imply a complete meal.
Native GUI checks cover both models with two profiles and the 1–4 profile controls; headless population performance excludes GUI and startup.
In the Male CNS four-individual trial, one individual consumed no food while the other three consumed the shared supply; the test proves conservation and isolation, not equal feeding.
